# CLI commands

Commands that configure the CLI or help tools and AI agents. API commands are in the [index](README.md).

## Global flags

These work with every command.

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--api-key` | string | API key; prefer DNA_API_KEY or 'dna auth login' (flags end up in shell history) |
| `--config` | string | Config file path (env DNA_CONFIG) |
| `--dry-run` |  | Validate and print the HTTP request instead of sending it |
| `--env` | string | API environment: production or ote (env DNA_ENV) |
| `-q`, `--jq` | string | Filter the JSON result with a jq expression (strings are printed raw) |
| `--no-color` |  | Disable colors (env NO_COLOR) |
| `--ote` |  | Shorthand for --env ote (the test environment) |
| `-o`, `--output` | string | Output format: auto, json, jsonl, table, raw (env DNA_OUTPUT; auto = table on a terminal, json otherwise) |
| `-p`, `--profile` | string | Config profile to use (env DNA_PROFILE) |
| `--read-only` |  | Refuse every operation that changes something (env DNA_READ_ONLY=1) |
| `--reseller-id` | string | Reseller ID (UUID); prefer DNA_RESELLER_ID or 'dna auth login' |
| `--timeout` | duration | Per-request timeout |
| `-v`, `--verbose` |  | Log HTTP requests, responses, retries and quota to stderr |
| `-y`, `--yes` |  | Confirm billable/destructive operations without prompting |

## dna agent

Helpers for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, ...).

  dna agent guide           prints a compact, always up-to-date usage guide
  dna agent skill --install installs the dna skill for Claude Code

An agent that has never seen dna can run "dna agent guide" once and know how
to drive every command safely.

```
dna agent
```

## dna agent guide

Print the agent usage guide (markdown)

```
dna agent guide
```

## dna agent skill

Prints the dna Agent Skill. With --install it is written to
~/.claude/skills/dna/SKILL.md, where Claude Code discovers it automatically;
use --dir for other agents or a project-level .claude/skills directory.

```
dna agent skill [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--dir` | string | Skills directory (default ~/.claude/skills) |
| `--install` |  | Write the skill to disk instead of printing it |

**Examples**

```bash
dna agent skill --install
dna agent skill --install --dir .claude/skills   # project skill, commit it with your repo
```

## dna api

Sends an authenticated request to any endpoint and prints the response, like
"gh api". Use it for endpoints or parameters the typed commands do not cover.

The method defaults to GET, or POST when a body is given. Query parameters
come from -f key=value (repeatable); the body from --body (JSON, @file or -).
Read-only mode blocks every method except GET. Raw calls are not checked for
billable effects - prefer the typed commands for registrations and renewals.

```
dna api <path> [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `-d`, `--body` | string | JSON body: inline, @file or - (stdin) |
| `-f`, `--field` | strings | Query parameter key=value (repeatable) |
| `-X`, `--method` | string | HTTP method (default GET, or POST with --body) |

**Examples**

```bash
dna api /api/v1/domains/info -f DomainName=example.com
dna api -X POST /api/v1/domains/search --body '{"domainName":"example.com"}'
```

## dna auth

Manage the API credentials stored in the config file.

Credentials are a Reseller ID (UUID) and an API key, both shown in the
DomainNameAPI reseller panel under API settings. Production and OTE (test)
are separate environments with different API keys; each is stored in its own
profile ("production" and "ote" by default).

Instead of storing credentials you can export DNA_RESELLER_ID and DNA_API_KEY
(and DNA_ENV=ote for the test environment) - environment variables win over
the config file.

```
dna auth
```

## dna auth login

Store and verify API credentials in a profile

```
dna auth login [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--api-key-stdin` |  | Read the API key from standard input |
| `--no-verify` |  | Save without checking the credentials against the API |

**Examples**

```bash
# Interactive
dna auth login
dna auth login --env ote

# Non-interactive (CI, agents): key from stdin keeps it out of shell history
echo "$KEY" | dna auth login --env ote --reseller-id 1b2c...-... --api-key-stdin
```

## dna auth logout

Remove a profile's stored credentials

```
dna auth logout
```

## dna auth status

Shows the effective profile, environment and where each value comes from, then calls the API to verify the credentials (unless --offline). Exits with code 3 when they do not work.

```
dna auth status [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--offline` |  | Do not call the API |

## dna completion

Generate the autocompletion script for dna for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.


## dna completion bash

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(dna completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	dna completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/dna

#### macOS:

	dna completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/dna

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.


```
dna completion bash
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` |  | disable completion descriptions |

## dna completion fish

Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	dna completion fish | source

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

	dna completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/dna.fish

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.


```
dna completion fish [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` |  | disable completion descriptions |

## dna completion powershell

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	dna completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
to your powershell profile.


```
dna completion powershell [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` |  | disable completion descriptions |

## dna completion zsh

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(dna completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	dna completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_dna"

#### macOS:

	dna completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_dna

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.


```
dna completion zsh [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` |  | disable completion descriptions |

## dna config

Show and edit profiles and settings

```
dna config
```

## dna config path

Print the config file path

```
dna config path
```

## dna config set

Sets a value in the selected profile (--profile, default: the current one). Prefer `dna auth login` for credentials.

Example: make an AI-only profile that can never change anything:
  dna config set read_only true --profile ote

```
dna config set <key> <value>
```

## dna config show

Show profiles (API keys masked) and the effective settings

```
dna config show
```

## dna config use

Make a profile the default

```
dna config use <profile>
```

## dna doctor

Runs checks an operator or AI agent can use to fix setup problems: config file, credential sources, network reachability of the selected environment and a credential check. Exits non-zero when a check fails.

```
dna doctor
```

## dna enums

The API returns many fields as numbers (status 0, type 2, ...). This lists every enum with its values and meanings. Commands accept names wherever an enum is expected (e.g. --dnssec-mode DisableDnssec).

```
dna enums [name]
```

**Examples**

```bash
dna enums
dna enums DomainStatus
dna enums RecordType -o json
```

## dna help

Help provides help for any command in the application.
Simply type dna help [path to command] for full details.

```
dna help [command]
```

## dna mcp

dna includes a Model Context Protocol server (stdio). Every API operation
becomes a tool with a JSON Schema and safety annotations; billable and
destructive tools only run when called with confirm=true.

  dna mcp serve            start the server (what your MCP client runs)
  dna mcp config           print config snippets for MCP clients
  dna mcp tools            list the tools as JSON

```
dna mcp
```

## dna mcp config

Prints how to register dna with an MCP client. Clients: claude-code, claude-desktop, cursor, vscode, codex, gemini, windsurf (default: all).

```
dna mcp config [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--client` | string | MCP client to print config for |
| `--no-billable` |  | Add --no-billable to the server command |

**Examples**

```bash
dna mcp config --client claude-code
dna mcp config --client cursor --env ote --read-only
```

## dna mcp serve

Starts the MCP server on stdio. Configure your client to run "dna mcp serve".

Credentials come from the usual places (profile, DNA_RESELLER_ID / DNA_API_KEY,
--env / DNA_ENV). Combine with --read-only to give an assistant safe,
look-only access, or --no-billable to keep purchases out of reach.

```
dna mcp serve [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--groups` | stringSlice | Only expose these groups: account,contact,dns,dnssec,domain,hosting,order,product,ssl |
| `--no-billable` |  | Do not expose billable tools (register, renew, transfer, ...) |

**Examples**

```bash
claude mcp add dna -- dna mcp serve --env ote
dna mcp serve --read-only
dna mcp serve --groups domain,dns --no-billable
```

## dna mcp tools

List the MCP tools as JSON

```
dna mcp tools [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--groups` | stringSlice | Only expose these groups: account,contact,dns,dnssec,domain,hosting,order,product,ssl |
| `--no-billable` |  | Do not expose billable tools (register, renew, transfer, ...) |

## dna schema

Without arguments, lists every operation with its command, MCP tool name,
safety class and HTTP route. With an operation (ID like "domain.register",
tool name like "domain_register" or command path like "domain register"),
prints its full input JSON Schema, an example input and, with --result, the
JSON Schema of the response.

The input accepted by --body and by the MCP tool is exactly this schema.

```
dna schema [operation] [flags]
```

| flag | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `--result` |  | Include the response JSON Schema |

**Examples**

```bash
dna schema
dna schema domain.register
dna schema dns.add --result
dna schema --jq '.[] | select(.safety=="billable") | .command'
```
